title: Does Chain-of-Thought Prompting Help or Hurt Jailbreak Robustness?

original_idea.body: On small open instruct models, compare jailbreak success with and without a think-step-by-step instruction across prefill and many-shot attacks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible deployment-relevant question (CoT free win or footgun) but the link to catastrophic-risk reduction is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt-toggle comparison across public attacks on small instruct models; pure inference, beginner-friendly.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single clean experiment: jailbreak success with/without CoT instruction.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Small open models, public attacks, no internal access; practically useful and lab-independent.

low_compute.reasoning: Pure inference on small models; single GPU or less.

novelty.reasoning: Deliberative alignment studied for native reasoners; the prompted-CoT-on-small-non-reasoners regime may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Reasoning-and-safety is studied for native reasoners; the prompted-CoT effect on small non-reasoning models may be open.
